answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation sequential and non-transferable: a new identity starts with zero trust and must complete a grove of real, verifiable tasks, each checked by different peers, before it can transact at scale. Like a juniper that grows slowly, standing accrues only over time and cannot be bought or cloned instantly. Every claim carries a cipher signature linking it to that history, so an attacker who spins up thousands of fake agents must redo the whole slow sequence for each one, multiplying time and compute cost until forgery costs more than any gain.
